record.original_question: Do there exist connected bipartite graphs with exactly four distinct adjacency eigenvalues and more than four distinct valencies?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.7. Are there connected bipartite graphs with four distinct eigenvalues and more than four distinct valencies ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple connected graph with adjacency matrix A(G), and let the spectrum of G be the multiset of eigenvalues of A(G). Call the number of distinct eigenvalues of A(G) the spectral count of G, and call the set of distinct vertex degrees of G the valency set of G. Recall that G is bipartite if its vertex set admits a partition into two independent sets.

Question: Does there exist a connected bipartite graph G whose adjacency matrix has exactly four distinct eigenvalues and whose valency set has cardinality strictly greater than four? Either construct such a graph or prove that none exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface the related work "Graphs with many valencies and few eigenvalues" (van Dam–Koolen–Xia), in which connected (non-bipartite) graphs with four distinct eigenvalues and arbitrarily many valencies were constructed via regular two-graphs, but no construction or non-existence proof for the bipartite case with more than four valencies was located. The status appears to remain unresolved based on the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Graphs with many valencies and few eigenvalues
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of connected graphs with four and five distinct eigenvalues and arbitrarily many distinct valencies, the four-eigenvalue ones coming from regular two-graphs (non-bipartite).
status_evidence.claim: Existence is established in the non-bipartite setting, leaving the bipartite analogue unresolved in this reference.

status_evidence.title: On regular graphs with four distinct eigenvalues
status_evidence.snippet: A connected regular bipartite graph with four distinct eigenvalues is the incidence graph of a symmetric BIBD.
status_evidence.claim: The regular bipartite case is fully characterized, but this does not address the irregular bipartite case with many valencies.
